cards.why: The ELD unit, serial VT-ELD-55107, was returned at Vessmoor's Joliet terminal on 21 August, and the receipt signed by its terminal manager says so (L-5). The escrow may be applied to equipment not returned (lease 9.2(c)); this was returned, and Vessmoor attached no document behind the charge (376.12(h), (k)(6))

A trailer washout fee is not an item the lease names: 9.2 lists fuel card purchases, tolls and scale tickets, equipment not returned, the plate and Schedule A chargebacks, and Schedule A names no washout. At return the carrier may deduct only obligations previously specified in the lease (376.12(k)(6)); a terminal policy is not the lease

The lease lets either party end it on 30 days' notice with no fee or penalty (L-1), Marcus gave that notice (L-4), and section 9.2 names no termination fee. A handbook page is not the lease, and keeping escrow as a penalty for leaving is not a deduction 376.12(k) allows

Vessmoor held the $2,500 for the whole of the third quarter, 1 July to 30 September 2026 (92 days), after the lease ended too, and posted no interest. Lease 9.4 and 376.12(k)(5): at least quarterly, at the investment rate of the last 13-week bill auction before 1 July, 29 June 2026, 3.828%: $2,500 x 3.828% x 92 / 365 = $24.12

The lease ended on 21 August 2026, so the escrow was due back by Monday 5 October 2026, 45 days later (376.12(k)(6); lease 9.5), and nothing has arrived: not even the $569.65 Vessmoor's own statement admits. The balance owed is $2,500 less only the deductions the lease allows, D-1, D-2, D-6, D-7 and D-8 ($985.35): $1,514.65. Valued at the $569.65 Vessmoor admits but has not paid; the $945 disputed is counted on the disputes
